text: Welcome to week 11 of the official
Arkham and Arca iRacing series. And this
week you'll be racing at the Bristol
Motor Speedway for 70 laps. You won't
have much time to warm your tires up in
qualifying this week, so you'll want to
get up to speed and heat them up through
your first lap.
Roll around the outside and avoid
scrubbing your tires as you make your
way around the track to take the white
flag.
As you hit the start-finish line to take
your final lap, lift and drag the brakes
to get the nose pointed into the turn
one. Give the car half a second to
settle against the inside and get back
on the throttle.
You hit it right, you should be able to
exit the corner without squaring off
your exit.
Take a breath and hit turn three with
the same energy. Drag the brakes ever so
slightly, roll the inside, wait just a
moment longer to get back on the
throttle and exit turn four.
The outside wall comes up slightly
quicker on this end of the track, so be
careful as you finish your run.
Let's see that again.
Once the race begins, starting in second
gear, your first priority should be to
guard the outside to the best of your
ability. If you have good track position
at the start, you can afford to run the
bottom with tire conservation in mind.
But if you're anywhere but the first two
rows, the outside line will prove to be
the stronger line.
If you get caught on the inside with a
line of cars on your outside, find a
hole and take it as soon as possible.
The tire conservation effect of the
inside line will be compromised by your
inability to use the full width of the
track. So prioritizing track position on
the start will be in your best interest.
It'll be tempting to go full bore once
you get to that outside lane, but you'll
need to fight that and allow the car to
roll through the corners as the tires
heat up. I'm not saying to put around up
there, but you'll want to back up your
entries and let the car rotate on its
own.
Once you found your rhythm and the field
has spread out slightly, start running
the inside as I mentioned earlier. The
outside may be faster, but the inside is
quicker. As long as you avoid pushing up
the track in the center, your tires will
appreciate you running the inside in the
corners and arcing out to the walls on
the straightaways.
As the leaders' tires heat up, the
inside will become a viable place to
pass. You'll need to build momentum and
take note of the traffic behind you
before you make your move.
If you weren't absolutely sure that you
can pull it off, regroup and give it
another shot. As a poor attempt will
open you up to attack by the freight
train of cars running the outside behind
you.
If the leaders insist on rolling the top
through the entirety of the race, they
will fall off dramatically toward the
end. So if you manage your tires from
the beginning, you will be able to beat
them.
If you can stay patient, keep your front
bumper intact, plan ahead before you
make your moves, you might find yourself
scoring good points leading into the
final week of the season. Good luck.
